Structures are explained here step by step, so they can be judged before capital is committed.

HAYKALAH explains the structures it works with in plain language, in Arabic and English. Start with a step-by-step explainer, the monthly Structuring Brief or the Knowledge Center, or use a tool to find where your own mandate starts. Everything here is general information. Nothing on this page is an offer, a solicitation or investment advice.

Saudi Structuring & Sukuk Review 2026

The Saudi Structuring & Sukuk Review 2026 is HAYKALAH’s annual report, in Arabic and English, free to read. It is in preparation and has not been published yet.

Saudi Structuring & Sukuk Review 2026 مراجعة الهيكلة والصكوك في السعودية 2026

In preparation

What it will cover

  • The market: how structuring and Sukuk work in the Kingdom today, drawn from published sources such as regulators, the exchange, industry bodies and rating agencies, each one cited.

  • The structures: Sukuk and the Shariah contracts behind them, such as Ijara, Istisna’a, Musataha and Wakala, alongside funds, joint ventures and public-private partnerships.

  • Assets into income: how land, buildings and facilities are structured to earn recurring income and support refinancing.

  • HAYKALAH’s perspective: lessons and playbooks from HAYKALAH’s archive, 2004–2026, with every client anonymized.

The Structuring Brief

The Structuring Brief explains one structure each month in plain language: what it is, when it is used, how it combines with other structures and where it appears in HAYKALAH’s work. Each issue is also published on this website.

Issues

  • Issue 1: Musataha The right to build on and use another party’s land for an agreed term, and how it combines with Istisna’a and Ijara

Explainers

Each explainer steps through one structure: who the parties are, what passes between them, and what has to be in place for it to work.

  • Proposal Stadium Sukuk (Proposal) How a stadium could be financed through Sukuk while the landowner keeps the land, through Musataha, then Istisna’a, then Ijara. A proposal with no mandate
  • Framework or proposal stage The asset-monetization engine How an idle asset moves through Audit, Optimize, Structure, Operate and Monetize to earn recurring income
  • General structure Sukuk al-Ijara How a lease-based Sukuk pays its holders from rent, from the transfer of the asset to its repurchase at maturity

Illustrative structures. Not an offer or investment advice. Shariah structures are subject to Shariah board approval.

Tools

Three tools help you find your own starting point. None of them asks for your name, and none of them gives investment advice.

  • Structure Finder Answer two questions, who you are and what you need, to see the practice, the structures and the cases that fit
  • Asset readiness check Five questions, one for each step of the engine, show where an asset should start. Not advice, not a valuation
  • Beta Ask HAYKALAH (Beta) Ask a question and get an AI-generated answer drawn only from HAYKALAH’s published pages, with numbered sources

Not investment advice.

Questions

Has the Saudi Structuring & Sukuk Review 2026 been published?

Not yet. It is in preparation. To hear when it is published, subscribe to the Structuring Brief.

Is anything on this page investment advice?

No. The explainers, the Brief, the glossary and the tools are general information. Nothing on this website is an offer, a solicitation or investment advice, and Shariah structures are subject to Shariah board approval.

Why is the stadium explainer labelled Proposal?

Because it is one. HAYKALAH proposed the stadium precinct Sukuk framework in 2026, and it has no mandate. Its figures are withheld until the source documents are reconciled.

How do I stop receiving the Structuring Brief?

Use the unsubscribe link in any issue.

Found a structure that fits? Tell us about the mandate. We can start under an NDA.
